transcript:
User: Hi. Saw your ad. Honestly I doubt this is for us but go ahead.
Agent: Got it — and I appreciate you being honest. When a call comes in and you or your team are tied up, what usually happens to that call?
User: We already have an answering service that handles those calls for us.
Agent: Got it, so you’re already paying for an answering service. Mhm — where does that setup still fall short for you, if at all (things like missed messages, slow pickup, cost)?
User: Well, they sometimes miss calls after hours or during busy times, which isn't ideal for our patients.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense — missed calls aren’t great, especially for patients. Roughly how many calls a week would you say end up missed or going to voicemail?
User: We miss about 10 calls a week. But again, we already have a service for this.
Agent: Makes sense, you’ve already got something in place. Has anyone ever walked you through what those 10 missed calls a week are actually costing you in patient revenue?
User: No, but I assume some of those missed calls could have booked. What's this going to cost? Give me a number.
Agent: Totally fair question — and yeah, some of those would’ve booked. Before we get into pricing, mind if I do a super quick calculation on what those 10 missed calls a week could be worth to your practice?
User: Honestly, I need a number now or I'm done. Just give me a ballpark figure for similar services.
Agent: Got it, you’re busy and want the straight answer. For practices using tech to stop missed-call loss, you’re typically looking at somewhere in the low four figures per month, depending on call volume and setup — does that range feel completely out of bounds for you, or potentially workable if it actually turned those 10 missed calls a week into booked patients?
User: Okay, that range is workable. But how do I know this isn't some sketchy startup that disappears with our patient data?
Agent: Yeah, that’s a totally valid concern — especially with patient data in the mix. When you think about “not sketchy,” what matters most to you: how long we’ve been around, how we handle HIPAA/PHI, or who actually has access to your patients’ information?
User: HIPAA compliance is crucial. How do you ensure data protection and what are your credentials or history in this field?
Agent: Yeah, that makes total sense — if HIPAA’s not airtight, nothing else really matters. We’re built specifically for medical practices: data’s encrypted in transit and at rest, access is locked down to your team, and we operate under a formal BAA so responsibilities are clear — would it help if Jay, our founder, walked you through our HIPAA setup and history with other clinics in more detail?
User: Alright, that sounds better. But I tried one of these AI things last year, it was garbage and wasted time.
Agent: Mhm, I hear you — a bad AI experience can sour the whole thing. Compared to what you tried last year, what specifically went wrong: was it how it talked to patients, the accuracy, or that it just didn’t actually book or help anyone?
User: It was inaccurate and didn't help book any appointments, just wasted three months of our time.
Agent: Got it — three months of bad data and no appointments would frustrate anyone. So with that in mind, let me ask this: if you could keep your current answering service but have missed calls and after-hours covered in a way that reliably books patients, would that actually be valuable enough to fix, or is this more of a “nice to have” for you right now?
User: If you can truly increase bookings and avoid past issues, it would definitely be valuable to us.
Agent: That helps, thanks for being straight about that. So with those 10 missed calls a week… ballpark, what percentage of those would actually book an appointment if someone answered — maybe half, around 50%, or would you put it higher/lower?
User: I'd say around 40% would book if someone answered promptly.
Agent: Got it, about 40% makes sense for a practice like yours. And when those patients do book, what’s a typical value of that visit for you — roughly how much revenue per new appointment?
User: On average, each new booked appointment brings in about $700 in revenue for us.
Agent: So with your numbers, those missed calls are costing you about $12,100 a month in potential revenue. Since this is meaningful and you’ve had a bad AI experience before, how about we do a focused 20‑minute walkthrough this week where Jay shows you exactly how we protect data and turn those missed calls into real bookings — would later today or tomorrow work better for that?
User: Tomorrow afternoon works. Call me at +16025550017 to set up the walkthrough. Thank you.
Agent: Perfect, tomorrow afternoon works. Quick thing before we lock this in — what’s your first name?
User: Brenda. And remember, call me at +16025550017, not the other number. Looking forward to it.
Agent: Got it, Brenda — I’ll note that number as your best contact. And what’s the name of your practice?
User: Desert Bloom Dental. Just ensure everything’s set for the call tomorrow afternoon. Thanks for accommodating my concerns.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that on our calendar for tomorrow afternoon.
Agent: Thanks, Brenda! You’re all set for tomorrow afternoon with Jay at Dialux — you’ll get an SMS confirmation with the details, and you can add it to your calendar or reschedule if anything changes. Is there anything else I can help you with before we wrap up?
